Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine shouldn’t have “equal rights” because rights are generally granted to persons—beings capable of interests, experiences, or moral agency—not beverages. But if you mean red versus white wine, there’s no ethical reason to discriminate based solely on color; preferences and regulations should apply fairly to both.

Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine isn’t a person or legal agent, so it doesn’t have “rights” in the human or civil-rights sense. It can be regulated—like other alcoholic beverages—because of health, safety, age restrictions, and public-order concerns, not because it is “red.” Humans, regardless of preferences about wine, should be treated equally.
